skill.name: video-inpainting
skill.description: Guides agents through RunComfy video inpainting workflows for object removal, region repair, and prompt-driven edits across frames.
skill.summary: Route video region edits through RunComfy models with practical prompt and CLI guidance.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Static hits are largely false positives from Markdown backticks, fenced CLI examples, documentation links, and disclosed RunComfy token storage. I found no prompt injection or hidden command execution, but the skill explicitly promotes watermark removal, which creates a medium business-logic abuse risk unless authorization is enforced.

remediation.issue: Watermark removal can enable unauthorized rights bypass.
remediation.suggestion: State that users must only remove marks from media they own or are authorized to edit. Ask for confirmation when rights are unclear.

remediation.issue: RunComfy processing sends source media or media URLs to an external service.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before uploading private or third-party video. Keep the endpoint allowlist and privacy notes visible.

content.value_statement: Video editors need a repeatable way to repair or replace regions across moving footage. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through RunComfy routing, prompt design, and CLI-safe workflow choices.
actual_capabilities: Routes region edit requests to RunComfy models such as Wan 2-7, Lucy Edit Restyle, and Seedream edit-sequential.
Provides runcomfy CLI examples with JSON input and output directory usage.
Helps write spatial prompts for removing objects, repairing regions, or replacing elements across frames.
Explains when mask-driven ComfyUI workflows are needed instead of CLI endpoints.
Summarizes exit codes, token setup, and outbound endpoint expectations for RunComfy use.
limitations: Requires an installed and authenticated RunComfy CLI.
Sends source media or media URLs to RunComfy services.
Prompt-driven edits may drift on precise masks or long clips.
Does not verify media rights or edit authorization.

use_cases.title: Clean Product Clips
use_cases.description: Repair unwanted visual artifacts in short product videos while preserving the rest of the scene.

use_cases.title: Repair Production Footage
use_cases.description: Choose a RunComfy route for removing visible distractions or replacing a region across multiple frames.

use_cases.title: Prototype Frame Stack Edits
use_cases.description: Plan sequential still-frame edits when a clip can be processed as a small frame stack.

prompt_templates.title: Remove a Region
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a simple object removal request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use video-inpainting to remove [object] from [video source]. Preserve all other content exactly and save results in ./out.

prompt_templates.title: Replace an Object
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for a controlled replacement across frames.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use video-inpainting to replace [object] with [new object]. Keep camera motion, lighting, and surrounding content consistent.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Best Route
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for selecting between available RunComfy models.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Wan 2-7, Lucy Edit Restyle, and Seedream edit-sequential for [clip details]. Recommend the safest route and explain limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Masked Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for precise region control.
prompt_templates.prompt: I need pixel-precise mask propagation for [region] in [clip]. Identify whether CLI editing is enough or a ComfyUI workflow is required.

output_examples.input: Remove a small distraction from the lower left corner of a short product clip.
output_examples.output: Recommended Wan 2-7 Edit-Video with a spatial prompt, preservation instruction, and local output folder.

output_examples.input: Edit a low-frame-rate clip as separate still frames.
output_examples.output: Recommended Seedream edit-sequential with a warning that temporal consistency can degrade on longer clips.

output_examples.input: Need exact mask tracking for a moving object.
output_examples.output: Recommended a RunComfy ComfyUI workflow instead of the CLI endpoint because precise masks require propagation.

best_practices: Use explicit spatial language and request preservation of all unchanged content.
Process one edit per pass to reduce drift across frames.
Confirm that the user owns or is authorized to edit the source media.
anti_patterns: Do not combine several unrelated edits in one prompt.
Do not use prompt-only routing when pixel-precise mask control is required.
Do not upload private or third-party video without explicit approval.

faq.question: Does this skill edit videos directly?
faq.answer: It guides an agent to use RunComfy models and CLI workflows. RunComfy performs the actual processing.

faq.question: Which model is the default route?
faq.answer: The skill defaults to Wan 2-7 Edit-Video for prompt-driven region edits.

faq.question: Can it handle exact masks?
faq.answer: Not through the CLI route. The skill recommends ComfyUI workflows for pixel-precise mask propagation.

faq.question: Does it require a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. The RunComfy CLI must be installed and authenticated before processing requests.

faq.question: Where are outputs saved?
faq.answer: The examples use a local output directory selected by the user or agent.

faq.question: Is private media uploaded?
faq.answer: RunComfy processing requires source media or URLs. Users should approve uploads before processing sensitive videos.
